main: Figure 4 | EvoState generalizes across K. pneumoniae lineages and resolves population-associated acquisition patterns. A, Global genome sampling. B, Top-14 resistance-state profiles, counted from sample-level binary barcodes. C, EvoState minus training-gain-frequency baseline single-gain log-likelihood for strictly held-out STs with at least 20 single-gain transitions. Points and whiskers show ST means and within-ST paired transition-bootstrap 95% intervals; the horizontal line and band show the ST-equal mean and whole-ST bootstrap interval. Split STs are excluded. D, Full model-implied acquisition-step distributions from the global model, sorted by expected model step. All 22 model distributions are shown as ridges individually scaled to their own peak; ridge heights are not comparable across features. Dots mark model expected acquisition steps computed from unscaled probabilities. Colors continuously encode those expected steps (earlier to later), not discrete biological stages. Empirical distributions and original model probabilities remain available in source data. E, Empirical expected-step offsets for the most supported STs, ordered by hierarchical clustering. The top dendrogram shows acquisition-pattern similarity, not genetic ancestry: correlation distance, average linkage and optimal leaf ordering, using features with at least five gains in at least 70% of STs. Unsupported entries are feature-median-imputed for clustering only; the heatmap retains all 22 features and original values and missing cells. F, Country-associated offsets for all 22 characters, identical to Supplementary Fig. S4D in values, row and column order, and color limits. E/F use the same global empirical reference; red means later, blue earlier. In both E and F, grey denotes zero reconstructed gain events, for which empirical acquisition order is not estimable; all cells with at least one local gain event are colored without point overlays. Right bars show mean absolute deviation across groups with estimable order; n counts those groups. Row-label and bar colors encode resistance mechanism class, not statistical significance. Low-support counts remain available in source data. Grey does not imply absence of the feature from sampled genomes. Country columns are grouped by continent for navigation, not inferred clusters. The ARI test uses the original 19-character filtered matrix (at least 30 global gains and not classified as insufficient data), in the original plot column order with seed=0 and 2000 permutations. F retains the original within-continent clustering and color limits, not recalculated when expanding the display to all 22 rows; missing deviations are zero-filled only for clustering. Acquisition step is not time; geographic and lineage effects are not disentangled.
S1: Supplementary Figure S1 | Sampling structure and resistance-state diversity of the global K. pneumoniae dataset. A, Country-by-recorded-isolation-year counts with marginal global totals; unknown years are explicitly retained. B, Top-28 profiles, displaying all 22 binary resistance characters. These are genome counts, not transition frequencies; rarer profiles are available in source data.
S2: Supplementary Figure S2 | Robustness of cross-lineage generalization. A, Total and single-gain transition support for main-panel STs. B, Absolute mean log-likelihood for EvoState and the gain-frequency baseline on identical transitions. C/D, Per-ST gain versus genome and single-gain transition counts across the same strictly held-out STs with at least five single-gain transitions and a recorded genome count. Grey points have 5–19 transitions and blue points at least 20. Spearman correlations are recalculated in this filtered cohort; threshold 1/2/5/10 sensitivity and unfiltered lineage results are supplied as source data. E, Sensitivity to minimum support thresholds 10, 20, 30 and 50, showing ST-equal bootstrap estimates and transition-weighted means. Bootstrap uncertainty is descriptive and does not model phylogenetic or shared-training-fold dependence.
S3: Supplementary Figure S3 | Lineage-specific model-implied distributions of resistance-character acquisition order. A–F, ST258, ST11, ST15, ST147, ST512 and ST307. Filled ridges are Monte Carlo acquisition-order distributions from separately fitted ST models, not Bayesian parameter posteriors. Only model distributions are shown; each ridge is scaled by its own model peak, so heights cannot be compared across features. Raw model probabilities and empirical distributions remain available in source data. A fixed blue-to-red palette follows the global empirical feature ordering and is shared across S3 and S4E–J; color does not encode group-specific acquisition time. All 22 characters and full 1–22-step support are retained, including model extrapolation beyond empirical support. This is in-sample characterization, separate from held-out performance.
S4: Supplementary Figure S4 | Country-associated heterogeneity in resistance-acquisition dynamics. A, Coverage of country-stratified analysis. B, PCA of empirical character-by-step matrices, colored by continent. C, Across-country standard deviation of expected acquisition steps for characters supported in at least five countries. D, All 22-character empirical deviations from the global reference; grey cells have no reconstructed gain events (empirical order not estimable), and all cells with at least one gain retain their deviation color without point overlays. Right bars show mean absolute deviation across countries with estimable order, with n indicating the number of such countries; row-label and bar colors encode mechanism class. Column order and color limits are inherited from the original 19-character country plot D, as in Fig.4F. E–J, Separately fitted country-model acquisition-order distributions for USA, China, UK, Italy, Thailand and India. Only model-filled distributions are shown, each scaled by its own peak; ridge heights cannot be compared across features. Empirical distributions remain in source data, and model trajectories may extend beyond empirical support. Cluster–continent ARI and PCA-score group tests concern different hypotheses; neither establishes geographic causation or independence from lineage composition.
